samples.summary: New `slides.slide.delete` reuses the alias `slide.delete`, which an earlier entry (`slides.delete`, delete the whole deck) already claims — `getCommandSchema` returns the first match, so `slide.delete` still resolves to the destructive document delete.
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts:281 — `slides.delete` (safety: 'destructive', 'Delete a slide deck') declares `aliases: ['slide.delete', 'deck.delete', 'decks.delete']`. The new entry at :395 declares `aliases: ['slide.delete', 'deck.slide.delete']`. Resolution is `registry.find((c) => c.name === name)` then `registry.find((c) => c.aliases?.includes(name))` (registry.ts:1409-1413) — first-wins, so the new alias is dead and an agent asking for `slide.delete` meaning "remove one slide" is handed the schema for deleting the entire presentation. Same shadowing risk applies to the pattern generally; only this one collides today.

samples.summary: Comment threads/replies/resolutions created through the new API never emit a notification: the notification pipeline is driven exclusively from the browser client, so participants and @mentioned users are silently not told about agent-authored comments.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/components/comments/notify.ts:125 `notifyCommentEvent()` is what plans and POSTs `comment_added` / `comment_reply` / `thread_resolved` reports (via `reportCommentNotification`, packages/frontend/src/api/notifications.ts:94) into packages/backend/src/notification/notification.service.ts. The new `createThread` / `reply` / `setResolved` handlers write straight into the Yorkie CRDT and call nothing in NotificationService, so every notification type the dropdown shows for a comment is skipped for API writes. The controller's own docblock even asserts the author identity is "the same identity the notification routes hold a comment reporter to", but no report is made.

samples.summary: `apply()` assigns the entire `root.slides` array (round-tripped and migrated through `MemSlidesStore`) for a single-slide operation, clobbering any concurrent per-slide/per-element edit the live editor made between the read and the write — contrary to the stated rationale that these verbs avoid whole-deck rewrites.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts mutates slides/elements granularly inside `doc.update` (per-element field writes), which is what makes concurrent editing converge. The new path does `doc.update((root) => { root.slides = result.slides; })` where `result.slides` came from `new MemSlidesStore(document)` — and `MemSlidesStore` clones + `migrateDocument`s on both construction and `read()` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:140-157), so every slide object in the deck is replaced wholesale, not just the one added/moved/deleted. Any collaborator edit landing during the request is lost, which is exactly the failure mode `PUT .../content` has and that this controller's docblock claims to avoid.

samples.summary: `comment-ops.ts` is a second, independent implementation of the frontend's comment CRDT helpers; the two will drift and already differ in surface (no `applyEditComment` backend-side, different function signatures).
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:1-145 already implements `toYorkieMs`/`fromYorkieMs`, `copyAuthor`, `copyComment`, `copyThread`, `applyAddThread`, `applyAddReply`, `applyDeleteComment`, `applyResolveThread` with identical semantics (including the index-0-deletes-the-thread rule and the bigint Long boundary). The backend copy takes a `ThreadMap` instead of a `Worksheet` and omits `applyEditComment`, so a future change to the Yorkie timestamp boundary or the delete rule must be made in two places; the frontend copy is also referenced by packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.ts:578 as the canonical description of that boundary.

samples.summary: `BoardDocument`/`BoardMeta` is a third hand-maintained copy of the board root shape; a field added to either of the other two will silently be dropped by `writeBoardRoot`.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/types/board-document.ts:3 `YorkieBoardRoot` and packages/board/src/model/board.ts:22 `BoardModel` both declare `{ meta: { title, unit?, recentColors? }, elements }`. `writeBoardRoot` rebuilds `meta` from an explicit field list (title/unit/recentColors), so any meta field added to the editor's root later is deleted by the next API write rather than preserved.

samples.summary: `duplicateTab` copies only `kind`/`datasourceId`/`query` from the source `TabMeta`, dropping `lakehouseSourceId`, `lakehouseRef` and `asOf` while preserving `type: 'lakehouse'`.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/lakehouse-view.tsx:74-76 reads `tab.lakehouseSourceId` / `tab.asOf` as the source of truth for the tab; a duplicate of a lakehouse tab would render as a lakehouse tab with no source. Currently likely unreachable because lakehouse/datasource tabs are created without a `sheets` entry (packages/frontend/src/app/documents/document-detail.tsx:398-423) and the controller refuses to duplicate a tab with no worksheet — but the meta copy is field-listed rather than derived, so it will be wrong the moment such a tab has a grid.

samples.summary: `PUT images` replaces the whole per-tab image map, so a concurrent editor insert/move of another image on the same tab is discarded.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-object-layer.tsx:50 reads `root.sheets[tabId].images` and the editor writes individual entries; the new handler does `ws.images = {}` then re-adds only the payload's entries. Consistent with the documented `charts` replace semantics, so flagged only as a nit.

The new entry at :395 declares `aliases: ['slide.delete', 'deck.slide.delete']`. verdict.reason: The finding is accurate as stated. `slides.delete` at registry.ts:274-281 already claims alias `slide.delete` (safety 'destructive', deletes the whole deck), and the new `slides.slide.delete` at registry.ts:387-395 declares the same alias. `getCommandSchema` (registry.ts:1409-1413) resolves by `registry.find(...)` on names then aliases, which is first-wins in array order, and `slides.delete` appears earlier in the array, so `slide.delete` resolves to the deck-level destructive delete and the new alias is dead. There is no uniqueness check: a repo-wide grep for `alias` in packages/cli returns only the `aliases` literals and the optional field on the type at registry.ts:36, and packages/cli/test/schema.test.ts (alias assertions at :184-219) never exercises `slide.delete`. The path is reachable: packages/cli/src/commands/schema.ts:43 feeds user input straight into `getCommandSchema` and prints the result, so an agent asking for the per-slide delete contract is handed the deck-delete schema (`doc-id` only, response `{ id }`). This is a shadowed/misresolving symbol outside the changed hunk with a live consumer — in-lane for blast radius and blocking at major.

finding.summary: Comment threads/replies/resolutions created through the new API never emit a notification: the notification pipeline is driven exclusively from the browser client, so participants and @mentioned users are silently not told about agent-authored comments.

The new `createThread` / `reply` / `setResolved` handlers write straight into the Yorkie CRDT and call nothing in NotificationService, so every notification type the dropdown shows for a comment is skipped for API writes. The controller's own docblock even asserts the author identity is "the same identity the notification routes hold a comment reporter to", but no report is made.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: the new comments controller injects only DocumentService and YorkieService (comments.controller.ts:83-86) and its createThread/reply/setResolved handlers mutate the Yorkie CRDT with no notification call (157-264); ApiV1Module neither imports NotificationModule nor provides NotificationService (api-v1.module.ts:38-77), so it cannot reach it indirectly. Repo-wide, the only producer of comment notifications is NotificationService.createFromComment, called solely from NotificationController POST /notifications/comment (notification.controller.ts:63-71), which is itself JwtAuthGuard-only — so an API-key caller cannot even self-report. On the client, notifyCommentEvent (notify.ts:125) is invoked only from local write paths (sheet-view.tsx:905/924/945, pdf-comments-controller.ts:43/62/86, docs-comments-controller.ts:286/318), never from a remote-change subscription, so no connected peer backfills for API writes. I also followed indirect chains and ruled them out: the Yorkie event webhook (yorkie-event.controller.ts:41-75) only touches Document.updatedAt and template review sync; comment-ops.ts has no notification hook; no cron/scheduler path creates notifications. Blast-radius relevant because the new endpoint is a second entry point to the same CRDT mutation that skips the notification side effect every existing entry point performs, leaving the notification dropdown/badge/SSE consumers with no row for agent-authored comments or @mentions. Found no counterexample.

The new path does `doc.update((root) => { root.slides = result.slides; })` where `result.slides` came from `new MemSlidesStore(document)` — and `MemSlidesStore` clones + `migrateDocument`s on both construction and `read()` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:140-157), so every slide object in the deck is replaced wholesale, not just the one added/moved/deleted. verdict.reason: The described code exists verbatim: slides.controller.ts:174-176 assigns the entire `root.slides` array inside `doc.update`, and the array comes from `MemSlidesStore.read()` (slide-ops.ts:78, 95, 115, 131), which clones+migrates the whole deck on construction (memory.ts:144) and again on read (memory.ts:156) — so every slide object is replaced wholesale for a single-slide operation. The affected other site is real and documents the very invariant being violated: the live editor's Yorkie store mutates granularly via `r.slides.splice(...)` (yorkie-slides-store.ts:734, 793, 803) and moveSlide reorders in place with the comment "Reorder in place (no rebuild) so a peer concurrently editing this slide's children keeps its edit" (yorkie-slides-store.ts:827-829). Nothing guards the read→write window: YorkieService.withDocument attaches in Manual sync mode, runs the callback, and syncs with no lock or version check (yorkie.service.ts:50-60), and the routes are ordinary reachable REST endpoints. Whole-array replacement in Yorkie discards concurrent remote edits to the replaced subtree, which is the same last-write-wins hazard explicitly warned about for the whole-deck primitive (slides-tree.ts:87-91) and which the controller's docblock (slides.controller.ts:42-44) claims to avoid. In-lane as a violated invariant another module relies on; severity major (silent loss of collaborator edits on a reachable path).
